overview: Two endocrine glands located near each other in the neck but controlling completely different things — metabolism versus calcium balance.
genZNote: Thyroid: sets your body's overall metabolic pace. Parathyroid: quietly manages your blood calcium in the background.

aspects.label: Main Function
aspects.valueA: Regulates basal metabolic rate, growth, and development.
aspects.valueB: Regulates blood calcium and phosphate levels.

aspects.label: Location
aspects.valueA: A single butterfly-shaped gland at the front of the neck.
aspects.valueB: Four small glands embedded on the back surface of the thyroid.

aspects.label: Effect on Blood Calcium
aspects.valueB: PTH raises blood calcium — the opposite effect to calcitonin.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Calcitonin (thyroid) and parathyroid hormone (parathyroid) have opposite effects on blood calcium — a frequently tested contrast pair.
overlay.memoryTrick: Thyroid = metabolism. Parathyroid = calcium (think 'para' = alongside the thyroid, but a totally separate job).
overlay.commonMisconception: The four parathyroid glands are not simply smaller parts of the thyroid gland — they are functionally and embryologically distinct organs that happen to sit on it.
